answer: A bonding-curve admission market prices each new identity by how many seats are already held by its funding cluster: the first seat is cheap, the next costs double, and fees are burned. Clustering follows every inlet of coins back to shared sources, so N fake heads pay roughly 2^N. Honest newcomers with separate funds stay cheap, while a farm feeding from one cedar-lined account or a single quartz cold wallet pays steeply per head.
